quote: Canaccord Genuity has advised 2X, a leader in subscription-based marketing as a service (MaaS) and a portfolio company of Recognize, on its strategic secondary investment from Insight Partners, a global software investor.
status_event: Private; Insight Partners bought in through a secondary investment announced in March 2025, Recognize stays invested.
sources_checked: Willkie note 2026-06 on the Knownwell acquisition
notes: No source uses the word minority or majority. Basis for the verdict: the seller's adviser (Canaccord) and Willkie (2026-06, https://www.willkie.com/news/2026/06/willkie-advises-2x-on-acquisition-of-knownwell: "2X, a portfolio company of Recognize") both still describe 2X as Recognize's portfolio company after Insight came in, and the company release says Insight is "on board along with Recognize". Recognize's own entry was announced 2023-03-29 (Business Wire headline; Willkie note dated 2023-04). The same Willkie note says the Knownwell deal "values the combined company at more than $400 million" (below $1B). The dossier's other 2x headlines (IPO subscriptions, FrontRunner) are unrelated name collisions. GlobeNewswire could not be fetched; the identical release was read on 2x.com.

quote: Status: Acquired by Insight Venture Partners
status_event: Appriss Retail was acquired by Gemspring Capital in March 2025.
sources_checked: JMI Equity portfolio page (the prior investor)
Form D of Alert Holding Company, Inc. 2015 (0001643449-15-000004)
notes: The citation is the portfolio page of JMI Equity, the investor that sold; the line sits under the Appriss entry. It is the seller's own site, not a data vendor; labelled press for want of a closer kind. Second source, GrowthCap 2019 (https://growthcapadvisory.com/growthcaps-top-40-under-40-growth-investors-of-2019/), on JMI's Bob Nye: "Appriss (acquired by Insight Venture Partners)". Form D 2015 of Alert Holding Company, Inc. (incorporated 2014, business combination box ticked) lists four directors, three of them at 1114 Avenue of the Americas (Parekh, Menzies, Agarwal); the issuer itself sits in Louisville, so it is not a formd_vehicle in the strict sense. PR Newswire 2019: "Clearlake will become an equal partner in Appriss alongside management and Insight Partners, which invested in Appriss in 2014." LABJ 2021: parent Appriss is "owned by Clearlake and Insight Partners". The 2014 announcement itself was not found. Priced event of $1B or more: the Appriss Insights unit was sold to Equifax for $1.825 billion, agreed 2021-08-10 (https://www.willkie.com/news/2021/08/appriss-equifax); that is a unit of the old group, not Appriss Retail. Appriss Retail was spun off in 2023; the old group's HQ was Louisville, KY. Clearlake.com returned 403 and could not be read.

GlobeNewswire and Asbury Park Press could not be read.

quote: Insight Partners, a global software investor, has joined Liberty Hall Capital Partners (“Liberty Hall”) [...] and Comply365’s current controlling shareholder, as an equal investor in the combined business.
status_event: Private; merged with Vistair in January 2024 and has bought Qualtero, ASQS, Rolls-Royce's safety management business, Beams and MINT since.
sources_checked: firm post 2024-06-04 (body on disk, release dated 2024-01-08)
notes: Joint control, for the judge to rule on. The [...] in the quote marks an omitted clause describing Liberty Hall; every word shown is the source's. Insight came in as an EQUAL investor next to the existing controlling shareholder, so Insight alone probably holds about half of the sponsors' stake and no source gives a percentage. Read under the rule 'together with a co-investor group': two private equity firms hold the combined company between them, which is control. Read as Insight alone: not established. Willkie (https://www.willkie.com/news/2024/01/willkie-advises-insight-partners-on-investment-in-connection-with-comply365-merger-with-vistair) uses the same words, "joins Liberty Hall Capital Partners as an equal investor in the combined business". A dossier headline dated 2020-12-15 (Business Journals, not opened) reports Comply365's earlier acquisition, which fits Liberty Hall's entry.

quote: Insight Venture Partners, a leading private equity firm in the area of software and technology investments, announces the acquisition of, and investment in, eCommerce Industries, Inc. (ECI2).
status_event: Acquired by The Carlyle Group in March 2014.
sources_checked: Willkie note 2014-03 on the Carlyle sale
notes: The citation is the deal note of Insight's law firm, headed "Leveraged Acquisition of eCommerce Industries"; labelled press for want of a closer kind. Sale as owner, Willkie 2014 (https://www.willkie.com/news/2014/03/eci): "Willkie advised Insight Venture Partners and ECi, an Insight portfolio company, in the sale of ECi". A WebSearch result summarised a Finextra press article (https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/10786/insight-venture-partners-acquires-ecommerce-industries) as saying existing investors NEA and Accel rolled over a minority; that page returned 403 and I could NOT read it, so it is a lead, not a quote. Later owners, from Google News headlines that were not opened: Leonard Green took a majority stake in 2020 (The Business Press, 2020-11-19) and Apax sold to it (Private Equity Insights, 2025-05-09). Several dossier headlines are about ECI Partners and ECI Technology Group, unrelated firms.

quote: Insight Partners invests over US $100M for majority control of iLobby
status_event: Private; the firm lists it as a current investment under its new name FacilityOS (no sale looked for beyond the dossier).
notes: SOURCES DISAGREE. The quote is the article's headline; its body only repeats the release and does not say majority again. Business Insider calls the same deal "a more than $100 million Series A funding round" led by Insight. The release itself says only "strategic investment", names three Insight board members (Hinkle, Agarwal, Malhotra) and a "buyside advisor to Insight Partners" (District Capital Partners), wording usual for a purchase. BetaKit: this was iLobby's first external financing. One trade publication's headline against one general outlet's round label; medium is the most this supports.

quote: said Jeff Lieberman, managing director at Insight Venture Partners, who was the majority owner of HealthcareSource.
status_event: Francisco Partners agreed to acquire HealthcareSource in April 2015; symplr bought it from Francisco Partners in 2021.
sources_checked: Form Ds of Healthcaresource HR, Inc. 2010
notes: Majority owner at the 2015 sale; the 2008 entry announcement was not found, so the entry itself is inferred. Willkie 2015 (https://www.willkie.com/news/2015/04/healthcaresource-acquired-by-francisco-partners): "Insight Venture Partners was the majority owner of HealthcareSource". Supporting: the Form D issuer Healthcaresource HR, Inc. is a Delaware company incorporated in 2008, the year Insight came in, which fits a holding company set up for the purchase; its 2010 board was the CEO, two Insight partners (Lieberman, Wells) and Stephen Ludwig. No earlier minority round by Insight is on record. The issuer's address is Woburn, not Insight's, so not a formd_vehicle.

quote: He declined to say if the deal gives Insight a control position
status_event: Private; agreed in September 2025 to sell its enterprise software business to Zeta Global for up to $325M, keeping Campaign Monitor, Emma and Vuture.
sources_checked: Form Ds of Campaign Monitor Holdings Pty Ltd 2014 and Campaign Monitor Holdings (UK) Ltd 2015
notes: The stake bought in 2014 was never disclosed; Fortune: "for an undisclosed ownership stake". Leans control, not settled. For control: Form D 2015 of Campaign Monitor Holdings (UK) Ltd (0000899140-15-000640) reports $398,574,622 of equity sold in a business combination, with Insight's Blair Flicker as Secretary and three of six directors from Insight; Willkie 2022: "The existing owners of CM Group, including Insight Partners, remain majority owners of the combined company"; Delimiter, citing the AFR, puts the deal at a $600 million valuation with a further US$160 million of debt. Against: $250M on a $600M valuation is about 42% if that figure is equity value; SMH 2019 says the founders "sold a large stake" and calls Insight "the company's biggest shareholder", not majority owner; the founders kept leading the company. The panel's first investment of November 2004 cannot be Insight's entry: the company was founded in 2004 and Fortune says Insight first contacted it in 2008. HQ was Sydney at entry; Nashville is from the firm's post of 2021-10-21 ("Headquartered in Nashville, TN, CM Group has United States offices in" several cities). Several dossier headlines are unrelated Marigold namesakes (a mine, a health startup, a caterer).

quote: In December 2005, investors led by Bain Capital Ventures and Insight Venture Partners acquired an aggregate of 67.8% of our outstanding capital stock from our original stockholders and we recapitalized our company.
status_event: Bought by Turn/River Capital in April 2025 for $4.4B, after being public 2009 to 2015 and again 2018 to 2025.
notes: The citation is the company's own IPO prospectus; labelled company_release. Control was bought by a GROUP led by Bain Capital Ventures and Insight, 67.8% together, so this is control under the co-investor-group rule, not Insight alone: the prospectus's stockholder table shows entities affiliated with Insight at 31.5% before the offering. Austin Ventures was not part of the December 2005 purchase; the prospectus says it bought shares from stockholders in December 2006. SOURCES DISAGREE on the date: Wikipedia says "During 2007, SolarWinds raised funding from Austin Ventures, Bain Capital, and Insight Venture Partners"; the prospectus and the firm's panel both say December 2005, and the prospectus is the primary source. The 2010 Form D is a small later issue with Jeff Horing as one director among eight, not a vehicle. Priced event of $1B or more: the $4.4B take-private announced 2025-02-07 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SolarWinds).

quote: The deal comes six years after Insight Partners acquired a majority stake in Tricentis for $165 million.
status_event: Private; GTCR invested $1.33B in November 2024 at a $4.5B valuation.
notes: SOURCES DISAGREE on the label, not on the facts. The firm and Willkie call the $165M "Series B financing"; three press pieces say that same deal bought control. QA Financial 2019-11-01 (https://qa-financial.com/tricentis-reaches-for-higher-testing-business/), an editor's bracket inside a CEO interview: "the private equity investment firm took control of Tricentis vi a $165 million financing" (typo in the source). QA Financial 2024-11-27 (https://qa-financial.com/tricentis-gets-1-3bn-vote-of-private-equity-confidence/): "with Insight Partners taking majority ownership in 2017" and "its majority shareholder, software investor Insight Partners". Wikipedia's infobox gives Insight 71%, citing Die Presse 2018. SiliconANGLE's 'six years' is loose arithmetic (2017 to 2024). The panel dates the entry November 2016, the announcement is 2017-01-23.  No earlier round by Insight was found. Priced event of $1B or more: $4.5B, 2024-11-26, same URL as the citation.
